questions.q:
With reference to India's defence industry, consider the following statements:
1. Defence Industrial Corridors have been set up in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
2. Items placed on the positive indigenisation lists cannot be imported after the deadlines set for them.
3. The United States, France and Armenia were the top three destinations of India's defence exports in 2023-24.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. The two corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu cluster defence manufacturers around anchor units and test facilities. Five positive indigenisation lists bar the import of over 5,000 items once their deadlines pass, which assures Indian makers of orders. The United States, France and Armenia led the 2023-24 list of buyers. Other levers include reserved capital budgets and the SRIJAN portal. Exports reached a record Rs 38,424 crore in FY 2025-26, against a target of Rs 50,000 crore by 2029.
questions.it: Defence industry policy and export markets

questions.q:
In the context of Indian defence products cited among recent exports, consider the following pairs of product and type:
1. BrahMos : Supersonic cruise missile
2. Akash : Surface-to-air missile system
3. Dornier-228 : Light transport and surveillance aircraft
4. Chetak : Main battle tank
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. BrahMos, an Indo-Russian supersonic cruise missile, has gone to the Philippines, which strengthens ties in the South China Sea. Akash is an indigenous surface-to-air missile for area air defence. The Dornier-228, built by HAL under licence, is a twin-engine utility aircraft used for transport and maritime surveillance, and has been supplied to neighbours. Pair 4 is wrong: Chetak is a light utility helicopter built by HAL. India's main battle tank is the Arjun.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 54; product types are static

questions.q:
With reference to reforms aimed at defence indigenisation, consider the following statements:
1. The SRIJAN portal invites industry and start-ups to manufacture items that the forces have been importing.
2. The 41 factories of the Ordnance Factory Board were merged into a single defence public sector undertaking.
3. The draft Defence Acquisition Procedure 2026 lowers the indigenous content requirement in order to attract foreign manufacturers.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. SRIJAN, launched in 2020, lists imported items so that Indian firms can offer to make them. Statement 2 is wrong: the factories were corporatised into seven separate DPSUs, each with its own product lines, such as munitions, vehicles and troop comfort items. Statement 3 is wrong: the draft raises the indigenous content requirement from 50 to 60 per cent for prioritised categories. Other levers include positive indigenisation lists, reserved capital budgets and industrial corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

questions.q:
With respect to the Mythos AI model and the concerns it raised in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was built mainly for defensive cyber security, including finding previously unknown vulnerabilities.
2. Access to it was restricted to about 40 organisations under Project Glasswing.
3. The Government of India set up a panel headed by the RBI Governor to assess the risks it poses.
4. Several Indian banks were among the organisations given early access to it.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The model can scan large codebases, chain several minor flaws into a serious exploit and do so faster than organisations can patch, which is why access went only to about 40 firms such as major cloud providers, chipmakers and US banks. Statement 3 is wrong: the panel is headed by the Chairman of the State Bank of India. Statement 4 is wrong: no Indian firm was among them, and India is in talks to join. Banks have been told to report incidents to CERT-In at once.

questions.q: In cyber security, a 'zero-day' vulnerability is
o: a flaw that has been publicly disclosed and patched on the day of discovery
a flaw unknown to the software maker, for which no patch exists when attackers first exploit it
a vulnerability that exists only in systems with no internet connection
an attack that wipes all data from a system on a fixed date
questions.e: The name means defenders have had zero days to fix the flaw, because it was unknown to the vendor until attackers or researchers found it. Such flaws are prized because no signature or patch can stop the first attacks. A flaw already disclosed and patched is a known vulnerability, and a timed wipe is a logic bomb. Frontier AI models that find zero-days quickly worry regulators because defenders may be overwhelmed, a concern for UPI and the banking system.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 58; concept is static

questions.q:
With reference to India's response to frontier-AI cyber risk, consider the following pairs of an instrument or body and its role:
1. AI Governance and Economic Group : Inter-ministerial body set up by NITI Aayog to coordinate AI policy
2. Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 : RBI's authority over payment system operators, including NPCI
3. Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 : Norms for handling personal data, relevant when breaches occur
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 3 are correct. The 2007 Act gives the RBI power to regulate and supervise payment systems, including NPCI, which runs UPI and would be central to any attack on digital payments. The 2023 Act sets duties on data fiduciaries, including breach reporting. Pair 1 is wrong: the AI Governance and Economic Group was set up by MeitY as the inter-ministerial apex body on AI policy. CERT-In, under MeitY, handles incident response, and NCIIPC protects critical information infrastructure.

questions.q:
In the context of AI-enabled tools in India's internal security, consider the following pairs of a tool and the body that runs or built it:
1. CCTNS 2.0 : National Crime Records Bureau
2. National IED Data Management Software : National Security Guard
3. Mulehunter.ai : Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre with IIT Bombay and the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub
4. Proactive Monitoring Tool for child sexual abuse material : CERT-In
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. CCTNS 2.0 uses AI to suggest applicable sections from FIRs, spot hotspots and link criminal profiles. The NSG's IED database applies language processing and image analysis to bomb data. Mulehunter.ai scores accounts used to route defrauded money. Pair 4 is wrong: the monitoring tool that screens cyber tiplines for child sexual exploitation material was developed by C-DAC Mumbai. The issue figured in the parliamentary committee report on the emergence of AI.

questions.q:
With reference to India's institutions against cybercrime, consider the following statements:
1. The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit, which tracks the dark web and unlawful deepfakes, functions under CERT-In.
2. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. The analytics unit sits within the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, not CERT-In; it follows data breaches, illicit marketplaces and cybercrime-as-a-service, and issues statutory takedown notices to social media intermediaries for unlawful deepfakes. As for statement 2, I4C is an attached office of the Ministry of Home Affairs, since policing is its business; it also runs the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline, where AI now classifies complaints. MeitY's agencies are CERT-In for incident response and the newer AI policy group.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 56; I4C under MHA is static

questions.q: The Directorate General of Analytics and Risk Management (DGARM), cited as an example of predictive governance using data analytics, functions under
o: the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
the Central Board of Direct Taxes
the Goods and Services Tax Network
questions.e: DGARM is a directorate of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs. It mines customs and GST data to flag suspicious patterns such as fake invoices and risky consignments, so officers can target checks instead of inspecting everyone. CBDT handles direct taxes through its own systems, the RBI regulates banks and payments, and GSTN is the technology company that runs the GST portal rather than an enforcement arm. The example appears in the debate on AI in administrative decision-making.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 57; DGARM under CBIC is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Algorithmic audits and keeping a human in the loop are recommended where AI is used in policing and administrative decisions.
Statement-II: AI systems trained on historical data can reproduce existing caste, gender or racial biases.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. Models learn from past records, so biased arrests or hiring decisions in the data become biased predictions, as with recruitment tools that favoured men. Because many models are black boxes, wrongful exclusion is hard to trace or appeal. Audits test outputs for skew, and human oversight keeps discretion and accountability where errors affect rights. The report also lists the digital divide and dependence on foreign technology as Indian concerns.

questions.q: Which one of the following examples cited in the debate on AI in governance is not correctly described?
o: CISF : centralised AI surveillance and AI-based baggage screening at airports
Bhashini : facial-recognition screening of passengers at airports by the CISF
eGramSwaraj : streamlines Panchayat planning and the use of funds
questions.e: The last description is wrong. Bhashini is the national language-technology mission that uses AI for translation and speech across Indian languages, cited as AI's inclusive side, though such tools also raise privacy questions. The other descriptions are accurate. eGramSwaraj is the Panchayati Raj platform for planning and accounts, e-challan standardises penalties by removing discretion, and the CISF uses centralised AI surveillance, predictive threat alerts and AI baggage screening at airports. Critics weigh such gains against algorithmic bias, black-box decisions and unclear accountability.

questions.q:
With reference to INS Aridaman, inducted in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was developed under the Advanced Technology Vessel programme with French assistance.
2. It is the third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine of the Arihant class.
3. Such submarines give India an assured second-strike capability, which underpins its no-first-use doctrine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Aridaman follows INS Arihant (2016) and INS Arighaat (2024) and is more advanced than both. A submarine at sea is hard to locate, so it can survive a first strike and retaliate; that is what makes a no-first-use posture credible and completes the land-air-sea triad. Statement 1 is wrong: the Advanced Technology Vessel programme, run for over three decades with DRDO and private industry, drew on Russian, not French, help. France is India's partner for Scorpene conventional submarines.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 59; Scorpene partnership is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarines are regarded as the most survivable leg of a nuclear triad.
Statement-II: Nuclear propulsion lets them stay submerged for very long periods, which makes them hard to detect and target.
Statement-III: India's nuclear doctrine permits first use of nuclear weapons against a large conventional military attack.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statements I and II are correct, and II explains I. Unlike diesel-electric boats, which must surface or snorkel to recharge batteries, a nuclear submarine can patrol hidden for months, so an adversary cannot be sure of destroying it in a first strike. Statement III is wrong: India's doctrine rests on no first use and credible minimum deterrence, with retaliation reserved for nuclear attack while keeping the right to respond to a major chemical or biological attack. INS Aridaman strengthens this second-strike posture.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 59; doctrine is static

questions.q:
Match the naval vessels delivered in 2026 in List-I with their description in List-II:
List-I
A. Malwan
B. Dunagiri
C. Sanshodhak
D. Agray
List-II
1. Stealth frigate of Project 17A
2. Large survey vessel for hydrographic work
3. Anti-submarine shallow water craft built at Cochin Shipyard
4. Anti-submarine shallow water craft built at GRSE, Kolkata
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Malwan is the second anti-submarine shallow water craft from Cochin Shipyard, named after the coastal town tied to Shivaji's maritime legacy. Agray is the fourth of eight such craft from GRSE, Kolkata, which shares the order. Dunagiri, also from GRSE, is the fifth Nilgiri-class stealth frigate of Project 17A with missile strike capability. Sanshodhak is the fourth large survey vessel for coastal and deep-water charting. Shallow water craft guard coastal approaches against submarines and mines.

questions.q: The Tunguska system, for which the Defence Ministry signed contracts in 2026, is
o: an Israeli loitering munition launched from ground vehicles
a long-range surface-to-air missile system for area defence of cities
a ship-borne close-in weapon system for destroyers
a Soviet-origin tracked air defence system combining surface-to-air missiles with twin 30 mm cannons against low-flying threats
questions.e: Tunguska, NATO name SA-19 Grison, is a self-propelled tracked system that travels with ground forces and protects them against low-flying aircraft. It pairs missiles with twin 30 mm autocannons, engaging targets roughly 8 to 10 km away, which suits it to helicopters, drones and cruise missiles. Long-range area defence of cities is the job of systems such as the S-400. It is a land system rather than a ship-borne one, and it is not a loitering munition.

questions.q:
With reference to the Remotely Piloted Strike Aircraft (RPSA) programme, consider the following statements:
1. Ghatak, developed under it, is a stealth unmanned combat aerial vehicle with a flying-wing design.
2. It is a programme of the Indian Navy to develop carrier-based drones for fleet defence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Ghatak's tailless flying-wing shape reduces radar signature, letting it penetrate heavily defended airspace for deep strikes without risking a pilot. Unmanned combat aerial vehicles carry missiles or bombs, unlike surveillance drones. Statement 2 is wrong: the programme is for the Indian Air Force, which is preparing to induct unmanned stealth fighters under it. The navy's carrier needs are being met separately, including through the twin-engine deck-based fighter project.

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS), consider the following statements:
1. Its chair rotates every two years by consensus among members.
2. India assumed its chairmanship in 2026.
3. France is a member because it holds territory in the Indian Ocean.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. IONS is a voluntary forum of navies from the Indian Ocean region, started by India in 2008. Membership is open to any state with permanently held territory abutting or within the Indian Ocean, which is why France, holding Réunion and Mayotte, is a member; there are 25 members. The chair rotates every two years, and India took it in 2026, hosting the IONS Maritime Exercise table-top exercise at Kochi.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 60; India's founding role and French territories are static

questions.q:
In the context of military exercises in the news in April 2026, consider the following pairs of exercise and participants:
1. Cyclone : India and Egypt
2. Dustlik : India and Kazakhstan
3. Surya Kiran : India and Nepal
4. Dosti : Coast guards of India, Maldives and Sri Lanka
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Cyclone is a joint special forces exercise with Egypt, whose fourth edition was held in 2026. Surya Kiran is the army exercise with Nepal. Dosti is a trilateral coast guard exercise among India, the Maldives and Sri Lanka. Pair 2 is wrong: Dustlik is held annually with Uzbekistan, alternating between the two countries. India's exercise with Kazakhstan is Prabal Dostyk, so the similar names make this a common confusion.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 61; Dosti and Prabal Dostyk are static
